_comment: Product-owner decisions of review/README.md §4, overlaid on source/ by convert.py (source/ is never edited). Entries under decisions 3, 7, 13, 14, 15, 16 and 18 are product-owner-delegated authoring (R1.4): the product owner asked the spec author to write them and reviews them in review/CATALOGUE.md.

_decisions.answer: Keep the four stable names; change the filter in a separate fix: the whole-word rule of bugfix/profanity-whole-word-matching, which must be merged before Task Group 2 (merged to main in PR #528, 4fd40c6d; spec 55 must be rebased on main before Task Group 2).
Discard all 7 alternatives (Northstar, Ramattra, Phineas Ratchet, Foxy, Black Lion, Platinum, Lead); no backup blueprints; every slot keeps its main blueprint.

Author franchise-flavoured team names for every stable and distinct robot names for the numbered robots, with their own art briefs; unit designations only where the franchise mass-produces identical units or the designation is canon.
Accept for now, rewrite with backlog #61.

Raise the robots target to the blueprint count wherever the spare blueprint is a good candidate, with the Booking Office target the larger roster needs (Paragon goal 8 → 2 and goal 3 → L4; Duo goal 13 → 3 and goal 11 → L6; Trio goal 12 → 4; Generalist goal 14 → 4). All 20 spares qualify; no spare blueprint is added or kept idle. Supersedes 'Accept: no spare blueprint per stable'.
Confirm the generated plans, re-confirmed against the spec-55 code as built.
Fix the three labels as recommended and polish every franchise label to official title casing and the starter format.
Keep Gigolo Joe, David Mecha and the human-looking android briefs as they are, provided the names pass the whole-word profanity filter.
Accept both Metropolis stables.
Keep robot names containing a list word as is.
As recommended: the Coverage_Matrix stays defined by the 11 starters; the test asserts over the union of all entries plus one starter-only assertion.

'Approved': the Squadron stables become Trio stables with robots target 6 (targetOverrides {"12": 6}, within the Trio bounds 3–6); Trio's default Weapons Workshop target is kept (no {"20": 8}); plans are regenerated (decision 6). Squadron has no spec-55 equivalent, so its purchase order (recruit 4, fund 5 and 6 together), upgrade order 1,4,2,5,3,6, authored plans, Workshop L8 path and the strategy_personality / purchasing_plan / equipment_budget prose are dropped.

'Rename them. Stay as close to the original as possible': names that fail the built validators are transliterated to plain ASCII (German umlauts as their standard digraph, so 'Löwe' becomes 'Loewe'; other diacritics are dropped, so 'Śmiały' becomes 'Smialy' and 'Łowca' 'Lowca'), apostrophes and em dashes are dropped, and over-long names are shortened minimally.

Decision 3 applies to the collection unchanged: franchise-flavoured team names and distinct robot names with their own art briefs, designations only for mass-produced or canon units; names are chosen together with the portrait.

'Make them unique': stable names case-insensitive, robot names exact and normalised (lower case, letters and digits only), team names exact and case-insensitive, across the starters and every Expansion_Stable; an original product-owner name beats a decision-3/14-authored name (the authored one changes); where both are original the higher-numbered stable changes.

'Go for it': decision 7 applies to the collection: starter format 'Title' or 'Title — subtitle', official casing, no slash, parentheses, instruction, year, medium or authorship annotation; shared labels get a starter-format subtitle; root-sharing between subtitled labels of one franchise is accepted because the product owner's plan places several stables in one franchise.
'Keep them. They are metal on the inside': decision 8 applies to the collection: the actor-likeness briefs, M3GAN and the fan-work and web-fiction franchises are kept.

'Align images and names': every slot whose name or art brief a decision changed is checked against its portrait; name and brief follow the image (images are not regenerated) unless the image clearly shows the wrong robot, which is recorded as needing a new portrait.

'Why would it not work? This should be able to scale to 10000 Automatons': no activation cap; a read-only scaling investigation goes in review/SCALING.md; the heavy test runs every repository Catalogue_Entry whatever their number and records timing per automaton; engine changes for larger populations are open items for the product owner.
'Then don't hardcode it or update it. I do like to get informed of totals though': counts and ranges are derived from source/, and one generated Totals block reports them.
